neighbours.label: a title word about to be followed by 'General' (Attorney General, Director-General, Governor-General, Inspector General)
fire: Last week the state Attorney General announced a lawsuit against the drug maker.
The report was sent to the Director-General of the World Health Organization in Geneva.
Several senators urged the Attorney General to open a formal investigation.
During the ceremony the Governor-General of Canada read the speech from the throne.
Lawmakers asked the Inspector General to audit the agency's spending.
A letter signed by forty mayors asked the Attorney General to intervene.
Officials met with the Deputy Director-General of the trade organization on Monday.
The memo was written by the Solicitor General before the hearing.
quiet: Last week the state treasurer announced a lawsuit against the drug maker.
The report was sent to the head of the World Health Organization in Geneva.
Several senators urged the police chief to open a formal investigation.
During the ceremony the Prime Minister of Canada read the speech from the throne.
Lawmakers asked an outside accountant to audit the agency's spending.
A letter signed by forty mayors asked the governor to intervene.
Officials met with the deputy minister of the trade organization on Monday.
The memo was written by a senior lawyer before the hearing.

notes: Card: peaks on ' attorney'/' Attorney' x11, ' Director' x3, ' Governor' x2, ' in' x4, each right before General/general. The + pole's output promotes ' general'. Quiet items keep government/legal topic and titles but drop the X-General compound. Probe: ' Attorney' before General 0.55, 'defense attorney' 0.003, 'in general' only 0.03, so the test uses title compounds only.
